result.plainSummary: Publishing could be marked complete using evidence that only checks changes to an agreed spec.
result.summary: Independent eab32d2d-6c3c-84df-b831-9bcc13fd0152 spec review grounded in related pack (4 features, 22 claims, 1 proposed claim, 50 docs). UUID creation, origin-aware migration, immutable original provenance, staged retryable migration, passive projections and fresh current validation are coherent. The publishing acceptance mapping points to unrelated 505a71e7-37de-8e56-ae5c-467828201dba; correct it before snapshot preparation. Clarify correlation token and ancestor conflict handling within the existing migration scope.

findings.gap: eab32d2d-6c3c-84df-b831-9bcc13fd0152 acceptanceClaimIds 596b8830-61c6-887a-b6c3-9ae0561f2761/AC-4 maps only 505a71e7-37de-8e56-ae5c-467828201dba, whose live statement checks recorded changes to agreed specs, not organization NPM_TOKEN wiring or dry-run publishing. Existing pass evidence could therefore satisfy unrelated publishing acceptance.
findings.plainImpact: The work could be called complete without evidence that publishing uses the requested organization credential.
findings.fixProposal: Map AC-4 to a dedicated relevant publishing claim with dry-run and workflow evidence; represent account reauthentication as an explicit separate outstanding outcome rather than infer success from code tests.

findings.gap: The universal ban on caller-chosen persistent IDs does not distinguish stable requestId correlation tokens required by docs/architecture/agent-tools.md from operation-allocated entity identities.
findings.plainImpact: Agents could lose safe retry behavior if each retry has to request a new identity.
findings.fixProposal: Explicitly retain caller-stable operation request tokens while generating resulting entity UUIDs once per creation outcome.

residualRisks: Migration should reject conflicting edits of the same ancestor record unless a documented reconciliation resolves them; a shared identity alone does not reconcile divergent contents.
Freeze and reuse origin mappings across retries, including interrupted live publication; regenerated random mappings must not remap already transformed references.
The tool-built related pack has only generic worktree caution text and no actual sibling-path scan; branch integration must validate both explicit origin histories.
